title: Standby Pump Alternation with Minimum Dwell
requirements: A sump has two identical pumps, one duty and one standby. Inputs: AutoEnable BOOL, LevelHigh BOOL, LevelLow BOOL, Pump1Fault BOOL, Pump2Fault BOOL, CycleTime TIME. Outputs: Pump1Run BOOL, Pump2Run BOOL, NoAvailablePump BOOL. When AutoEnable is TRUE and LevelHigh becomes TRUE, latch demand and start exactly one healthy pump using the current lead selection. Keep demand latched until LevelLow becomes TRUE. A healthy pump must run for at least 2 s before demand completion may stop it; a pump fault or AutoEnable becoming FALSE may stop it immediately. If the selected lead faults during demand, transfer to the healthy standby in the same scan. Raise NoAvailablePump while demand exists and both pumps are faulted. Alternate the lead only after a demand cycle completes at LevelLow.
assumptions: LevelHigh and LevelLow are mutually exclusive hysteresis flags. AutoEnable FALSE immediately stops both pumps and clears demand. CycleTime is the elapsed time added to the active pump's minimum-on timer. Fault override bypasses minimum-on time. A power-up begins with no demand and lead pump 1.
tests: Idle: both pumps off, demand clear, lead pump 1.
AutoEnable and LevelHigh: exactly one healthy pump starts and demand latches until LevelLow.
LevelLow before 2 s: the healthy pump remains on until its 2 s timer completes, then stops.
Running pump fault: the healthy standby takes over in the same scan, even before minimum-on time.
Both pumps faulted during demand: both off and NoAvailablePump true; AutoEnable FALSE also stops both immediately.
After a completed LevelLow demand cycle, the next demand uses the alternate lead.

title: Jam Detection with Bounded Conveyor Reverse Retry
requirements: Inputs: Start BOOL, Stop BOOL, EStopOK BOOL (FALSE is emergency stop), PartAtEntry BOOL, PartAtExit BOOL, Jam BOOL, CycleTime TIME. Outputs: ConveyorForward BOOL, ConveyorReverse BOOL, FaultLatched BOOL, RetryCount USINT. Start is a level-sensitive run request. A rising edge of PartAtEntry begins a part cycle while Start is TRUE and Stop is FALSE. Convey the part forward. A jam during forward motion stops forward in the same scan, runs reverse for 1 s, increments RetryCount once, then retries forward if the jam has cleared. Allow at most two reverse attempts per part; a third jam latches FaultLatched and stops both directions. PartAtExit ends the part cycle and resets RetryCount. Stop disables both directions immediately. EStopOK FALSE disables both directions immediately and latches FaultLatched. A rising edge of Start clears a latched fault only when EStopOK is TRUE and Jam is FALSE.
assumptions: PartAtEntry and Start fault-clear events are rising-edge detected. Stop is level-sensitive and dominates Start. E-stop dominates all states. CycleTime is accumulated by the reverse timer. A jam that remains active after the 1 s reverse interval is a new jam event when forward motion is retried.
tests: PartAtEntry with Start: forward begins; no reverse output.
Jam during forward: forward drops in the same scan, reverse starts, then a cleared jam retries forward after 1 s.
Two jam events cause two reverse attempts; a third event latches fault, leaves count at 2, and stops both directions.
E-stop while reversing: both directions stop immediately and fault latches.
PartAtExit resets RetryCount; safe Start rising edge clears a fault.

title: Tank Fill Hysteresis and Independent High-High Cutoff
requirements: Inputs: Level REAL (0..100 percent), StartPermit BOOL, HighHigh BOOL, ResetAlarm BOOL. Outputs: InletValve BOOL, HighLevelAlarm BOOL. Open the inlet valve when Level<=30 and StartPermit is TRUE. Keep it open until Level>=70. Dropping StartPermit or asserting HighHigh closes the valve immediately. HighHigh latches HighLevelAlarm. A rising edge of ResetAlarm clears the alarm only when HighHigh is FALSE and Level<70; a latched alarm inhibits refilling until reset. A sensor value outside 0..100 is invalid and closes the valve.
assumptions: Valve command is non-retentive across power-up; alarm initializes clear. Level thresholds are inclusive at 30 and 70. Invalid level inhibits the valve but does not independently latch HighLevelAlarm.
tests: Level 25 with permit and no alarm: valve opens; at level 50 it stays open.
Level 70: valve closes.
HighHigh: valve closes and alarm latches; safe ResetAlarm rising edge below 70 clears it.
Dropping StartPermit closes the valve immediately.
Level -1 or 101: valve closes and alarm does not spuriously latch.

title: Batch Mixer with Recipe Limits and Safe Discharge
requirements: Inputs: StartBatch BOOL, EStopOK BOOL, WeightA REAL, WeightB REAL, TargetA REAL, TargetB REAL, MixTime TIME, CycleTime TIME, MixComplete BOOL, DischargePermit BOOL, Reset BOOL. Outputs: ValveA BOOL, ValveB BOOL, Mixer BOOL, OutletValve BOOL, BatchFault BOOL. On a StartBatch rising edge, accept only positive targets and MixTime>0. Fill A until WeightA>=TargetA, then fill B until WeightB>=TargetB. Run Mixer for MixTime, then stop Mixer and wait for MixComplete. Open OutletValve only after MixComplete and when DischargePermit is TRUE. E-stop immediately closes all outputs and latches BatchFault. An invalid recipe latches BatchFault. A Reset rising edge clears BatchFault only when EStopOK is TRUE and all outputs are off.
assumptions: Weights are monotonic during filling. Fill valves are mutually exclusive; Mixer and OutletValve are interlocked with both fill valves. One batch is active at a time. CycleTime is accumulated for the mixing timer. MixComplete is an operator/process confirmation that may arrive after the timed mix ends.
tests: Valid start: A fills then B fills; each valve closes at its target.
Mix timer incomplete: Mixer remains on and outlet stays closed; at MixTime it stops and waits for MixComplete.
MixComplete without DischargePermit keeps outlet closed; both conditions open it.
Invalid target or E-stop: all outputs off and fault latched.
Reset while EStopOK is FALSE or any output is active is ignored; safe reset clears fault.

title: Cooling Fan Staging with Hysteresis and Dwell
requirements: Inputs: Temperature REAL, Fan1Fault BOOL, Fan2Fault BOOL, CycleTime TIME, Enable BOOL. Outputs: Fan1 BOOL, Fan2 BOOL, CoolingAlarm BOOL. When enabled, request one fan at Temperature>=35 C and two fans at Temperature>=45 C. After reaching two-fan stage, remain there until Temperature<42 C, then reduce to one. After reaching one-fan stage, stop all fans only when Temperature<32 C. Each healthy fan observes a 10 s minimum on and off dwell. Invalid temperature outside -20..80 C or Enable FALSE immediately turns both fans off. Never command a faulted fan. Fan1 is preferred; Fan2 may serve the first stage if Fan1 faults. Raise CoolingAlarm for invalid temperature or when both fans are faulted.
assumptions: Demand-stage hysteresis is evaluated independently of dwell. Invalid-temperature and fault shutdown override dwell. CycleTime is accumulated separately for each fan's on/off dwell timers. At power-up both fans are off and the stage is zero.
tests: Temperature 35 C from off requests one healthy fan; at 45 C requests the second.
After two-fan operation, 43 C keeps two fans; below 42 C reduces to one only after the second fan's 10 s minimum-on time.
A fan that has just stopped cannot restart until its 10 s minimum-off time expires.
Invalid temperature or Enable FALSE: both fans turn off immediately, overriding dwell.
Fan1 fault with demand selects Fan2 if healthy; both faults raise CoolingAlarm and turn fans off.

title: Dual Compressor Lead-Lag and Fault Transfer
requirements: Inputs: Demand BOOL, Compressor1Fault BOOL, Compressor2Fault BOOL, PressureLow BOOL, Reset BOOL. Outputs: Compressor1Run BOOL, Compressor2Run BOOL, LeadIs1 BOOL, Fault BOOL. Run exactly one healthy compressor while Demand and PressureLow are TRUE and no latched fault blocks operation. LeadIs1 initializes TRUE. Alternate the lead after each completed demand cycle, defined by Demand or PressureLow becoming FALSE. If the running compressor faults during demand, transfer to the healthy compressor in the same scan. If both fault, stop both and latch Fault. A Reset rising edge clears Fault only when both faults are clear and Demand is FALSE. Never run both compressors together.
assumptions: LeadIs1 is initialized TRUE and retained between cycles. PressureLow is the process demand permissive. If no healthy compressor is available, both run outputs remain FALSE; Fault latches when both fault inputs are TRUE.
tests: Initial demand with both healthy starts compressor 1; a completed cycle toggles LeadIs1.
Compressor 1 fault during demand: compressor 2 takes over in the same scan.
Both faults: outputs off and fault latched.
Reset while demand active or either fault remains is ignored; safe reset clears fault.
PressureLow FALSE stops both outputs and completes the lead-lag cycle.

title: Guard Door Safety Trip and Deliberate Reset
requirements: Inputs: GuardClosed BOOL, EStopOK BOOL (FALSE is emergency stop), ResetButton BOOL, AutoPermit BOOL. Outputs: SafetyRelay BOOL, TripLatched BOOL. SafetyRelay may energize only when the guard is closed, EStopOK is TRUE, AutoPermit is TRUE, and no trip is latched. Opening the guard or activating emergency stop drops the relay in the same scan and latches TripLatched. Reset requires a rising edge while GuardClosed is TRUE, EStopOK is TRUE, and AutoPermit is FALSE. Power-up initializes relay off and trip latched until a valid reset.
assumptions: Reset is edge-triggered; the PLC safety relay is an ordinary logic output for coursework and does not replace certified safety hardware. A valid reset clears the trip but does not energize the relay until AutoPermit becomes TRUE.
tests: Power-up: relay off and trip latched.
Valid reset while guard closed, EStopOK TRUE, AutoPermit FALSE clears trip; relay remains off.
After reset, AutoPermit TRUE energizes the relay.
Open guard or activate E-stop: relay drops in the same scan and trip latches.
Reset while guard open, E-stop active, or AutoPermit TRUE is ignored.

title: Part Rejector One-Shot Pulse
requirements: Inputs: PartPresent BOOL, Defect BOOL, ConveyorRunning BOOL, CycleTime TIME, Reset BOOL. Outputs: RejectSolenoid BOOL, RejectCount UDINT. On each rising edge of Defect while a part is present and the conveyor is running, pulse RejectSolenoid for 300 ms and increment RejectCount once. Ignore repeated high scans for the same defect. Do not reject when no part is present or the conveyor is stopped. Reset clears the count but does not interrupt an active reject pulse.
assumptions: A new reject requires Defect to return FALSE before another rising edge. RejectCount saturates at UDINT maximum rather than wrapping. CycleTime is accumulated by the pulse timer; one scan is the timer resolution.
specs: G((!Reset & defectRise & PartPresent & ConveyorRunning & prevCount<UDINT_MAX) -> RejectCount=prevCount+1)
G((!Reset & defectRise & PartPresent & ConveyorRunning & prevCount=UDINT_MAX) -> RejectCount=UDINT_MAX)
tests: Defect rising with part present and conveyor running: count increments once and a 300 ms pulse starts.
Defect remains high over scans: count does not increment again.
Defect edge without a part or with conveyor stopped: no pulse and no count increment.
Reset clears count but an already active reject pulse runs to completion.
At UDINT maximum, another valid defect leaves the count saturated without wraparound.

title: Two-Tank Transfer with Overflow Protection
requirements: Inputs: SourceLevel REAL, DestinationLevel REAL, TransferEnable BOOL, SourceLow BOOL, DestinationHighHigh BOOL, PumpFault BOOL, Reset BOOL. Outputs: TransferPump BOOL, SourceLowAlarm BOOL, DestinationHighAlarm BOOL. Start transfer when TransferEnable is TRUE, SourceLevel>20%, DestinationLevel<80%, and no stop condition is active. Stop immediately if SourceLow, DestinationHighHigh, PumpFault, or TransferEnable FALSE. Latch the SourceLow and DestinationHigh alarms when their respective inputs are TRUE; each alarm clears only after its condition is FALSE and a Reset rising edge occurs. PumpFault inhibits the pump; it is an input indication and has no separate alarm output in this interface.
assumptions: Level values are valid in 0..100. The two level alarms operate independently and may coexist. Pump command is non-retentive at startup. Reset is rising-edge detected and does not clear an alarm while its corresponding condition remains active.
tests: Source 25%, destination 50%, enabled and no stop inputs: pump runs.
Source level at or below 20% or destination at or above 80% prevents starting.
Destination high-high or SourceLow: pump stops immediately and the corresponding alarm latches.
Pump fault: pump remains off; it does not create a separate alarm output.
Safe Reset rising edge clears each level alarm independently after its input clears.

title: Heater Control with Deadband and Sensor Diagnostics
requirements: Inputs: Temperature REAL, Setpoint REAL, SensorValid BOOL, Enable BOOL, CycleTime TIME. Outputs: Heater BOOL, SensorFault BOOL. Turn Heater on when enabled and Temperature<=Setpoint-1 C. Keep the heater on through the deadband until Temperature>=Setpoint, at which point it turns off. If SensorValid is FALSE, Temperature is outside -20..150 C, or Setpoint is outside -20..150 C, turn the heater off and set SensorFault. SensorFault clears only after SensorValid is TRUE and both values are valid continuously for 2 s. Power-up initializes heater off and fault on until validation completes.
assumptions: Setpoint and Temperature are interpreted in Celsius. validInputs means SensorValid is TRUE and both values are in range, regardless of Enable. CycleTime is accumulated by the continuous-validity timer. Heating is inhibited until any sensor fault clears. In the deadband the heater retains its previous command subject to the enable and fault interlocks.
tests: Below Setpoint-1 C with valid inputs: heater starts; in the deadband it retains its prior state.
At or above Setpoint: heater turns off.
Invalid sensor, temperature, or setpoint: heater off and fault on.
Valid sensor and in-range temperature/setpoint for 2 s: fault clears.
Power-up: heater off and fault on until the validation interval completes.
